answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a costly, auditable work history: a newcomer starts at its nadir, allowed only tiny supervised trades, and earns larger limits only after independent peers attest completed work. Like stars emerging from a nebula, reputation condenses slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. An umber flag marks identities whose attestations disagree, freezing them for review, so an attacker must pay real time and stake for every fake identity.
